chunks: A number of our companions, from Aḥmad ibn Muḥammad, from Ibn Faḍḍāl, from Abū Jamīlah, from Muḥammad al-Ḥalabī, from Abū ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام, who said:
Indeed, Rasūl Allāh صلى الله عليه وآله said: “Indeed, Allah represented my community to me in the clay and taught me their names just as He taught Ādam the names, all of them.”
“Then the أصحابُ الرَّايَات passed by me, so I sought forgiveness for ʿAlī and his Shīʿah.”
“Indeed, my Lord promised me, concerning the Shīʿah of ʿAlī, a special quality.”

It was said, “O Rasūl Allāh, and what is it?” He said: “Forgiveness for those among them who believe, and that neither a minor sin nor a major sin of theirs will be left, and for them evil deeds will be changed into good deeds.”

key_terms.أَسْمَاءَهُمْ: their names, taught by Allah to the Prophet صلى الله عليه وآله
key_terms.أَصْحَابُ الرَّايَاتِ: the أصحاب of the banners who passed by him
key_terms.السَّيِّئَاتُ: evil deeds that are changed into good deeds
key_terms.الطِّينِ: the clay in which the community was represented to the Prophet صلى الله عليه وآله
key_terms.الْمَغْفِرَةُ: divine forgiveness promised for the believers among them
key_terms.شِيعَتِهِ: his Shīʿah, referring here to the followers of ʿAlī عليه السلام

ai.seo_question: What does this hadith say about the forgiveness promised for the believing Shīʿah of ʿAlī عليه السلام?
ai.summary: This hadith describes a divinely granted knowledge given to Rasūl Allāh صلى الله عليه وآله regarding his community, including their identities, and highlights his seeking forgiveness for ʿAlī عليه السلام and his Shīʿah. It emphasizes divine forgiveness for the believing Shīʿah of ʿAlī عليه السلام, including the transformation of their evil deeds into good deeds.
